title: Control of information systems
blurb: Internal control, its components and IT controls.

topics.name: Internal control basics
topics.line: What controls are, why a business has them, and where they fall short.
topics.remember: Controls: policies and procedures. Reasons: minimise risk and ensure compliance. Limits: people, collusion, unusual transactions.
topics.simple: Internal controls are the rules a business sets to reach its goals safely. They cannot be perfect, and small firms have it hardest.
frames: shield
Controls are policies and procedures to achieve objectives.
target
They exist to minimise risks and make sure rules are followed.
alert
They have limits: people make mistakes, can work together to beat them, or face unusual transactions.
building
A small company has fewer employees, so its controls are weaker.
gls: a policy or procedure used to reach an objective
people working together to get around a control

cards.mean: Policies and procedures to achieve objectives
cards.ex: A rule that a payment needs approval.
Fewer losses and the rules are followed.

cards.mean: The human element, collusion and unusual transactions
cards.ex: Two staff agree to hide an error.

cards.mean: Weaker controls due to fewer employees
cards.ex: With only two staff, one person may do many jobs.

items.q: Two employees agree to hide an error

items.q: A one-off unusual transaction nobody expected

items.why: Minimising risks is a reason for controls.

items.q: Making sure the rules that apply are followed
items.why: Ensuring compliance is a reason for controls.

items.q: A person makes a simple mistake
items.why: The human element is a limitation.

topics.name: Components of control
topics.line: The building blocks of a control system, remembered as CRICM.
topics.remember: CRICM: Control environment, Risk assessment, Information and communication, Control activities, Monitoring
topics.simple: A good control system has several building blocks. Together they set the tone, find the risks, record events, act, and keep checking.
frames: building
The control environment sets the tone: governance and management attitudes.
search
The business finds and analyses its risks.
lock
Control activities stop problems (preventative) or find them (detective).
eye
Monitoring checks that the system still works.
gls: stops a problem before it happens
finds a problem after it happens

cards.ex: Managers show by their own behaviour that controls matter.

cards.mean: Oversee the control structure and reporting
cards.ex: A committee reviews how controls and reports are working.
Listing what could go wrong in the business.
Recording each sale as it happens.
Approval before payment, and review afterwards.
Checking regularly that controls still work.

items.q: Management sets an example of honest behaviour
items.why: Governance and management attitudes form the control environment.

items.q: Listing the risks the business faces
items.why: Identifying and analysing risks is risk assessment.
Capturing transaction events is the information system.

items.q: Approval before a payment is released
items.why: Preventative and detective controls are control activities.

nodes.s: oversee the control structure and reporting

topics.name: IT controls
topics.line: General IT controls for the whole setup, information processing controls for one application.
topics.remember: General IT controls: whole IT environment. Information processing controls: specific application.
topics.simple: General IT controls protect the whole IT set-up. Information processing controls protect one application and its data.
frames: key
Manage access: passwords stop unauthorised amendments.
gear
Manage change: program changes are tested and approved.
calc
Input and processing controls check completeness, accuracy and matching.
database
Master files use record counts and hash totals.
gls: general IT controls, for the whole IT environment
information processing controls, for a specific application
comparing batch totals before and after processing

cards.ex: A password stops an unknown person editing the ledger.

cards.mean: Testing and approval of program changes
cards.ex: A new payroll version is tested and approved before use.
Jobs run on schedule and the business can carry on after a failure.
Checking an entered batch is complete and correct.
Comparing totals before and after processing.
Counting records to see none are lost.

game.title: General IT control or processing control?

items.q: A completeness check on entered data

items.q: Scheduling and continuity of IT operations
items.why: Manage IT operations is a general IT control.

items.q: Record counts and hash totals on a master file
items.why: Master file controls are information processing controls.
